newsitem.title: UK: European, Gulf LPG soars as consumers caught short.
newsitem.headline: European, Gulf LPG soars as consumers caught short.

text.p: European, Middle Eastern and Asian liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) rallied strongly again this week as U.S. and east Asian demand drove Gulf premiums up and forced many European buyers onto the sidelines, traders said.

Shortages in key consumer markets, especially the United States, opened arbitrage windows from Europe to the United States, in turn attracting Gulf supplies into the Mediterranean and Mediterranean cargoes to northern Europe.
A week-long production problem in Norway's Kaarstoe terminal, which cut output by 60 percent, added to the bullish pressure, they said.
"With the problems in Kaarstoe, the high crude prices, low inventories in the States and the tension in the Middle East, there are lots of things making the price go up," a trader said.
The Kaarstoe terminal was brought back up to normal output on Friday, according to Statoil, but the other factors combined to keep the rally intact.
Large propane cargoes jumped by $20 to $240 cif NWE by Friday, although trade in Europe was thin as buyers were reluctant to accelerate the rally by showing their requirements.
European propane sellers, eyeing cif U.S. east coast prices of $270 cif, adjusted their sights upwards nevertheless.
U.S. buyers were paying 3-5 cents premium to Belview prices for winter supply cif east coast, and Gulf coast prices touched 50 cents per gallon on Friday.
"Everyone has started the winter season with very low inventories because prices during the summer were unusually high," a trader said.
"Now it's the start of winter and they have to buy regardless of the price."
Algeria was particularly keen to cash in on the low U.S. inventories and rising prices, traders said, having sold earlier in the week at $230 cif Flushing.
Rising demand in southern China was yet another bullish factor in the pot driving Gulf premiums up too.

Traders said Kuwait Petroleum Corp's second October tender for a 44,000-tonne mixed propane/butane cargo was awarded at $10.25 premium to October Saudi contract prices (CP). The first was awarded to Japan at around $5 premium.
This follows Saudi Arabia's first October tender awarded to a Swiss trader at $188.00 per tonne for propane and $200 for butane, $18-20 higher than the September contract price.

Saudi's second October sales tender closed on Friday, and traders expected it to be awarded around $200 for propane and $210.00 for butane. A spot Saudi cargo had changed hands in the meantime, but the price was kept secret.
Japanese prices talked around $35-40 premium to the CP for October loadings, while ballooning demand in southern China spiked prices up to Saudi CP +$70 delivered.
